title: Resources, configuration, native extensions and print mode

rows.operation: `/name <args>` parses quoted arguments before `$1..$N`, `$@` and `${N:-default}` substitution; `""` and `''` are retained as empty positional arguments and therefore do not shift later positions.
rows.consumer: `prompt-templates.ts:parseCommandArgs` and `expandPromptTemplate`; the session consumes the expansion in `AgentSession.prompt` before the model call.

scenarios: quoted-empty arguments are retained by the prompt argument parser
quoted-empty argument does not shift positional defaults in template expansion
session prompt expands the quoted-empty template before the model call

rows.cppEvidence: `tests/coding_agent/PromptTemplateProcessingTest.cpp` verifies quoted-empty argument retention (`[""]`) and preserves later positional parameters without shifting.
rows.recommendation: Track whether a token started, not whether its buffer is non-empty, and add the captured quoted-empty cases to the prompt processing test. Do not change the documented substitution forms in the same fix.

rows.capability: Prompt template positional, collection, default and slice substitution
rows.operation: `$1..$N`, `$@`, `$ARGUMENTS`, `${N:-default}`, `${@:-default}`/`${ARGUMENTS:-default}`, `${@:N}` and `${@:N:L}` substitution without recursive expansion.
rows.consumer: `prompt-templates.ts:substituteArgs`; the expanded text becomes the user message in `AgentSession.prompt`.

scenarios: positional, collection and default substitution forms
quoted-empty argument does not shift positional defaults in template expansion

rows.cppEvidence: Positional, collection, `${N:-default}`, `${@:N}`, `${@:N:L}`, `${@:-default}`, and `${ARGUMENTS:-default}` are implemented and tested in `tests/coding_agent/PromptTemplateProcessingTest.cpp`.
rows.recommendation: Add the two collection-default forms after the quoted-empty parser fix. Keep the existing no-recursive-expansion contract.

rows.capability: Prompt template discovery and explicit prompt paths
rows.operation: Load prompt templates from the agent/project `.pi/prompts` sources and explicit CLI prompt-template paths; a template named `review` expands `/review ...` at the session boundary.
rows.consumer: `DefaultResourceLoader` prompt selection and the CLI `--prompt-template` path; `AgentSession.prompt` expands the loaded template.

scenarios: session prompt expands the quoted-empty template before the model call
explicit resource paths load prompts, skills and themes

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/ProjectResourceLoader.cpp` prompt discovery plus the CLI `--prompt-template` path (`src/coding_agent/cli/CliParse.cpp:528`); expansion lives in `PromptExpansion.cpp`.
rows.cppEvidence: `tests/coding_agent/ProjectResourceLoaderTest.cpp:271-350` covers `--no-prompt-templates`, explicit prompt inputs and precedence; `tests/coding_agent/PromptTemplateLoaderTest.cpp` covers loading.
rows.recommendation: None for discovery; the quoted-empty expansion gap is tracked separately.

rows.operation: The first existing regular file among `AGENTS.override.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.MD`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.MD` wins in each directory; ancestor files load root-to-leaf and the agent-config file loads first.
rows.consumer: `resource-loader.ts:loadContextFileFromDir` and `loadProjectContextFiles`, consumed by `DefaultResourceLoader.getAgentsFiles` and the system-prompt project-context section.

scenarios: AGENTS.override.md wins over AGENTS.md and ancestor context is root-to-leaf

rows.cppEvidence: `src/coding_agent/ProjectResourceLoader.cpp` lists `AGENTS.override.md` first in `kContextFileCandidates`. `tests/coding_agent/ProjectResourceLoaderTest.cpp` verifies single-directory override precedence and root-to-leaf ancestor layering.
rows.recommendation: Add `AGENTS.override.md` as the first candidate and add the captured override-vs-AGENTS.md case. This is a v1.3.0 context-loader delta, not a new resource surface.

rows.operation: When cwd is inside a linked worktree nested under the main repository, the worktree's context file shadows the main repo's same-named file; the main repo copy is not loaded twice. Symlinked worktree paths are compared by canonical directory path.
rows.consumer: `resource-loader.ts:findShadowedContextFile` and `loadProjectContextFiles`.

scenarios: nested linked worktree shadows the main repo context file
worktree context file symlink is loaded once and not duplicated from the main repo

rows.cppEvidence: `tests/coding_agent/ProjectResourceLoaderTest.cpp:1181-1209` covers the nested-worktree copy; `:1211-1260` covers the no-worktree-copy and different-filename dedupe cases. The C++ test uses a synthetic git layout, while the capture uses real `git worktree add` metadata.
rows.recommendation: None. Keep the existing dedupe tests as the comparison seed; the capture adds real git metadata and the symlink observation.

rows.operation: Resolve explicit resource paths with tilde expansion, leading `@` handling, Unicode-space normalization, relative/absolute normalization and `file:` URL conversion; package-source prefixes (`git:`, `npm:`, `github:`, `http(s):`, `ssh:`, `builtin:`) bypass local resolution.
rows.consumer: `utils/paths.ts:resolvePath,isLocalPath` and `main.ts:resolveCliPaths` for `--extensions/--skills/--prompt-templates/--themes`; `InitialPrompt` separately handles `@file` and tilde expansion.

scenarios: local path modifiers expand tilde and strip a leading @
package source prefixes bypass local path resolution

rows.cppSeam: `src/agent/harness/WorkspacePathResolution.cpp:resolve_to_cwd` (Unicode spaces, leading `@`, `~`/`$HOME`, absolute/relative lexical resolution). Explicit `--skill`/`--prompt-template`/`--theme` paths call `absolutePath`, which uses this operation.
rows.cppEvidence: `src/coding_agent/environment/WorkspacePathResolution.cpp:resolveResourcePath` implements JavaScript trim, tilde expansion, POSIX file:// conversion, literal leading @, and preserves Unicode spaces. Explicit resource inputs resolve through this seam in `ProjectResourceLoader.cpp` and `SessionFactory.cpp`, verified in `ProjectResourceLoaderTest.cpp` and `ResourceReloadTest.cpp`.
rows.recommendation: Implement the selected path behavior in a bounded slice: convert `file:` URLs and preserve the upstream leading-`@` outcome for CLI resource flags, without changing the tool-path `@` convention. Keep ADR 0057's no-follow symlink and filesystem-authority rules. The shared `resolve_to_cwd` seam may need a resource-flag-specific normalization rather than a global behavior change.
rows.membershipAuthority: ADR 0075 §Selected capability additions — Application: resource/context paths; #1044 Implementation Decisions.

rows.capability: Explicit skill, prompt-template and theme path sources
rows.operation: Explicit paths load resources in addition to discovery; `--no-skills`, `--no-prompt-templates` and `--no-themes` drop discovery but keep explicit inputs.
rows.consumer: `DefaultResourceLoader` additional paths and the C++ `--skill`, `--prompt-template`, `--theme` flags.

scenarios: explicit resource paths load prompts, skills and themes

rows.cppEvidence: The C++ flags are singular (`--skill`, `--prompt-template`, `--theme`); the upstream plural flags are the same resource families. `--extensions`/`--no-extensions` are deliberately absent per ADR 0036 G1, and no arbitrary extension path source exists.
rows.recommendation: Keep the existing flag spelling; the third-party `--extensions`/`--no-extensions` loader remains excluded. Native extension behavior is selected separately through the same extension seam, not through a third-party plugin path.

rows.operation: The published `SettingsSchema` accepts the supported field shape and unknown top-level keys, and rejects invalid enum/range values; it includes resource-source fields (`packages`, `extensions`, `skills`, `prompts`, `themes`) and model/thinking/compaction/retry fields.
rows.consumer: `settings-schema.ts:SettingsSchema` (generated JSON Schema / repository config artifact), not the runtime `SettingsManager` loader.

scenarios: settings schema accepts the supported shape and unknown top-level keys
settings schema rejects invalid thinking level and negative compaction reserve

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/include/cch/coding_agent/Settings.hpp:UserSettings` and `src/coding_agent/SettingsManager.cpp:parse_settings` manual field parsing; there is no generated C++ `SettingsSchema` counterpart.
rows.cppEvidence: The C++ subset has typed fields for the model/thinking/session/shell/theme/compaction/retry/presentation values and rejects an invalid `defaultThinkingLevel` (`tests/coding_agent/SettingsManagerTest.cpp:195`). It does not publish a schema and has no typed fields or consumers for the selected local resource path lists (`skills`, `prompts`, `themes`). The third-party `packages`/`extensions` markers remain excluded.
rows.recommendation: Define a C++ settings contract for the fields the application actually supports, including the selected local resource path fields (`skills`, `prompts`, `themes`). Do not adopt the third-party `packages`/`extensions` markers by wholesale copying the upstream schema.
rows.membershipAuthority: ADR 0075 §Selected capability additions — Application: settings schemas for the actually supported fields and resource/context paths; #1044 Implementation Decisions.

rows.operation: `SettingsManager.create` merges global and project scopes; reads package sources and local resource path lists; reads model/thinking/enabled-model/compaction/retry fields; `reload()` re-reads changed values.
rows.consumer: `settings-manager.ts:SettingsManager` and the resource loader's settings-backed path selection.

scenarios: settings manager reads package and local resource paths and reloads changed values
settings manager consumes values the published schema rejects

rows.cppEvidence: C++ consumes the model/thinking/session/shell/theme/compaction/retry subset and reloads both scopes; `tests/coding_agent/SettingsManagerTest.cpp:437` covers reload. C++ does not consume the selected local `skills`, `prompts` or `themes` path lists. It also does not consume `packages`/`extensions`, which are explicitly excluded third-party package/TS-plugin surfaces. Unknown fields are preserved on surgical writes but ignored by the typed view (`:84`).
rows.recommendation: Keep `packages`/`extensions` excluded as third-party package/plugin surfaces. Implement the selected local `skills`/`prompts`/`themes` settings-path consumption in a bounded resource-path slice; keep the existing model/thinking/compaction/retry/theme-name reload behavior. Keep only the currently supported provider/model selection; this audit does not restore retired provider or model settings.
rows.membershipAuthority: ADR 0075 §Selected capability additions — Application: settings and resource/context paths; #1044 Implementation Decisions.

rows.operation: The runtime `SettingsManager` consumes a stored `defaultThinkingLevel: "bogus"` and spreads a string `packages` value into characters, even though `SettingsSchema` rejects both shapes.
rows.consumer: `settings-manager.ts` runtime getters, independent of `settings-schema.ts`.

scenarios: settings manager consumes values the published schema rejects

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/SettingsManager.cpp:parse_settings` validates selected fields (`defaultThinkingLevel`) and has no `packages` consumer.
rows.cppEvidence: C++ is not a copy of the upstream runtime bug: it rejects invalid thinking levels (`SettingsManagerTest.cpp:195`) and does not parse `packages`. Do not add validation behavior to match this upstream runtime acceptance.
rows.recommendation: Use `SettingsSchema` as the validation reference where a C++ schema is needed; do not mirror the runtime's unvalidated consumption.

rows.capability: Keybindings configuration parsing, migration and diagnostics
rows.operation: Load `<agentDir>/keybindings.json` with BOM stripping, legacy-name migration, valid-key filtering, unknown-action retention, conflict reporting and replace-all user binding semantics.
rows.consumer: `keybindings.ts:KeybindingsManager.create`/`getEffectiveConfig`; the interactive TUI dispatcher consumes the resolved registry.

scenarios: keybindings schema accepts unknown action ids with valid keys and rejects malformed values
keybindings manager migrates legacy names, keeps unknown actions, drops invalid values and reloads

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/tui/KeybindingsManager.cpp:load_keybindings_manager` and the diagnostics at `:301,321`; table in `app_keybinding_definitions`.
rows.cppEvidence: C++ reads only the Agent Config Directory, migrates known names, validates values, bounds diagnostics and reports conflicts. It diagnoses `unknown_action`/`unavailable_action` instead of retaining an unknown action in the user map; the upstream schema allows an unknown action id with a valid key value and the manager retains it without installing it. The C++ 43-action app table matches the upstream v1.3.0 43 `app.*` entries (`tests/coding_agent/tui/KeybindingsManagerTest.cpp:281`).
rows.recommendation: Align unknown-action handling with the upstream keybindings schema/manager: retain an unknown id in the user binding map, do not install an unknown action in the effective registry, and add a test for schema acceptance versus runtime absence. Keep the existing known-action, migration, BOM, conflict and reload behavior.
rows.membershipAuthority: ADR 0075 §Selected capability additions — Application: keybindings schemas for the actually supported fields; #1044 Implementation Decisions.

rows.operation: `/reload` re-reads `keybindings.json` and replaces the active user bindings; removed entries fall back to defaults.
rows.consumer: `KeybindingsManager.reload()` and the C++ `/reload` re-catalog path (`InteractiveEngine` keybinding re-catalog).

scenarios: keybindings manager migrates legacy names, keeps unknown actions, drops invalid values and reloads

rows.cppEvidence: C++ implements the re-catalog and replace-all behavior; `tests/coding_agent/tui/KeybindingsManagerTest.cpp` covers startup and diagnostics but not the reload transition specifically.
rows.recommendation: Add a C++ reload transition test seeded by the captured before/after bindings; no production change is implied.

rows.capability: Theme validation schema and runtime loading
rows.operation: `validateThemeJson` accepts a 56-token theme, rejects an unknown color token, a missing required token and a name containing `/`; `loadThemeFromPath` throws on an unknown token but accepts a missing required token and a slash name.
rows.consumer: `theme-schema.ts:validateThemeJson` for the published schema; `theme.ts:loadThemeFromPath` for runtime loading and `/reload`.

scenarios: theme schema accepts the 56-token built-in shape
theme schema rejects an unknown color token while runtime loading throws
theme runtime accepts a missing required token and a slash name that the schema rejects

rows.cppEvidence: C++ requires `text` and rejects a slash name, but accepts unknown color tokens passively (`ThemeTest.cpp:346` says `like pi`). It also accepts a missing required token with the schema wording test (`:264`). The runtime/schema split in upstream is not a single behavior to copy: the schema rejects unknown/missing/slash cases, while the runtime has the observed TypeError/missing/slash outcomes.
rows.recommendation: Re-pin the theme tests to the v1.3.0 schema: reject unknown color tokens, reject a missing required token, reject a slash name. Keep runtime loading's own error handling separate from the published-schema contract; do not copy the upstream runtime's missing-token acceptance.
rows.membershipAuthority: ADR 0075 §Selected capability additions — Application: theme schemas for the actually supported fields; #1044 Implementation Decisions.

rows.operation: The v1.3.0 theme token set has 56 entries: 51 required and optional `scrollbarTrack`, `scrollbarThumb`, `searchMatchBg`, `searchMatchText`, `thinkingMax` fallbacks.
rows.consumer: `theme-tokens.ts:THEME_TOKENS`, the published theme schema, built-in dark/light themes and runtime resolution.

scenarios: theme schema accepts the 56-token built-in shape

rows.cppEvidence: C++ has 53 tokens. Missing relative to v1.3.0: `scrollbarTrack`, `searchMatchBg`, `searchMatchText`. Required count (51) and optional `scrollbarThumb`/`thinkingMax` already match.
rows.recommendation: Add the three v1.3.0 optional tokens with their documented fallbacks (`muted`, `selectedBg`, `text`) and retain the existing required-token validation. This is a schema-shape delta, not a new theme UI feature.
rows.membershipAuthority: ADR 0075 §Selected capability additions — Application/TUI: theme schemas and complete token shape; #1044 Implementation Decisions.

rows.operation: Extension sources contribute model-facing tools through a registry; the runner converts each into the Agent's ordinary ToolRegistry path, preserving policy and collision rejection.
rows.consumer: The C++ Native extension seam; upstream equivalent is `registerTool`/loader/runner.
rows.cppEvidence: `tests/coding_agent/ExtensionToolSourceTest.cpp:181-319` covers registry collection, duplicate rejection, Agent ToolRegistry conversion, assembly visibility and callability. This is the implemented tool-source subset of the native extension behavior selected by ADR 0075 (§Selected capability additions, Extensions) and #1044. ADR 0066's #865 ruling bounds this tool-source slice only; it cannot narrow the later selected extension target. Direct third-party TS/JS execution remains excluded.
rows.recommendation: Extend this native seam with the selected hooks, run-triggering and prompt/busy-state behavior tracked in `extension-lifecycle-hooks`; do not add a TS/JS plugin loader.
rows.membershipAuthority: ADR 0075 §Selected capability additions — Extensions; #1044 Implementation Decisions. The #865 ADR 0066 ruling is only the historical tool-source foundation.

rows.operation: A `before_agent_start` handler observes a busy context (`ctx.isIdle() === false`), can replace the system prompt and inject a custom message; an extension `sendMessage(..., {triggerTurn:true})` from an idle session starts another run; the contributed message and tool result are retained across a tool turn.
rows.consumer: Upstream extension runner and `AgentSession._prepareRun`; the native C++ target is the selected registration/hooks/tool-wrapping/run-triggering and prompt/busy-state extension behavior.

scenarios: before_agent_start observes busy state and contributes prompt plus custom message
extension-triggered run starts from an idle session and retains contributions across a tool turn

rows.cppSeam: No general extension lifecycle hook. `src/coding_agent/AgentSessionExecution.cpp:401` only builds the MCP server system-prompt section; `ExtensionToolRegistry` is a tool-contribution seam, not a `before_agent_start`/`sendMessage` seam.
rows.cppEvidence: C++ has no `before_agent_start`, custom-message trigger, or extension-driven run API. The native extension tool seam is wired at Session Assembly, but no native extension lifecycle/runtime is present. ADR 0075 (§Selected capability additions, Extensions) explicitly selects native registration/hooks/tool wrapping/run triggering and prompt/busy-state semantics; #1044 includes the same native extension behavior. ADR 0066's minimal #865 tool-source ruling cannot veto this later membership decision. Direct third-party TS/JS execution remains excluded.
rows.recommendation: Implement bounded native slices: (1) extension registration/event dispatch and `before_agent_start` with busy/idle context; (2) system-prompt and custom-message contributions plus `sendMessage({triggerTurn:true})` run triggering; (3) tool wrapping and contribution retention across a tool turn with settled ordering. Reuse the existing Extension Tool Source registry; do not add a TS/JS plugin loader.
rows.membershipAuthority: ADR 0075 §Selected capability additions — Extensions: native hooks, registry, tool wrapping, run triggering and prompt/busy-state semantics. #1044 Implementation Decisions — Included native C++ extension behavior must support registration/hooks/tool wrapping/run triggering and correct prompt/busy-state lifecycle. Direct third-party TS/JS plugin execution is excluded.

rows.operation: Text mode prints only the final assistant text blocks; a completed `stop` response prints text and exits 0; a terminal `error`/`aborted` response writes a stderr diagnostic and exits 1.
rows.consumer: `print-mode.ts:runPrintMode` and the CLI `--print`/`--mode text` path.

scenarios: complete text response prints final text and exits 0

rows.cppEvidence: C++ prints final text blocks and handles Error/Aborted with stderr + exit 1; tests cover those outcomes and signal exit codes. `--mode json`/`rpc` are rejected per ADR 0036 G1.
rows.recommendation: None; the length-truncated branch is tracked separately.

rows.operation: A final assistant response with `stopReason: "length"` prints its partial text to stdout, writes `Response was truncated: the model reached its output token limit.` to stderr and exits 1.
rows.consumer: `print-mode.ts:runPrintMode` text branch.

scenarios: length-truncated text response prints partial stdout, warning stderr and exits 1

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/cli/PrintMode.cpp:print_final_assistant_text` handles only Error/Aborted, then prints every text block and returns true; `tests/cli/PrintModeTest.cpp` has no `length` case.
rows.cppEvidence: C++ has `AssistantStopReason::Length` in the shared AI type and an interactive warning in `AssistantMessageComponent.cpp:520`, but print mode does not test it. The captured upstream process result is stdout `partial answer\n`, stderr warning, exit 1; the C++ branch would currently print the partial text and exit 0.
rows.recommendation: Add the length branch to the print final-text outcome: print the partial text, write the exact warning to stderr and return exit 1; add a scripted C++ test matching the captured process outcome.

rows.operation: `--mode json` emits the session header/event stream; upstream has it, C++ rejects it.
rows.consumer: `print-mode.ts:runPrintMode` JSON branch.
rows.cppEvidence: ADR 0036 G1 explicitly rejects `--mode json` and `--mode rpc`; this is not a missing outcome of the supported text mode.
rows.recommendation: Do not restore JSON print mode under this audit.

rows.capability: System-prompt/docs/command claims about resources and extensions
rows.operation: Audit references and commands that could imply absent packages/extensions/themes/prompt-template capabilities.
rows.consumer: `SystemPromptBuilder.cpp:build_docs`, `BuiltinSlashCommands.cpp` and `docs/usage.md`/`docs/keybindings.md`.

scenarios: explicit resource paths load prompts, skills and themes

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/prompt/SystemPromptBuilder.cpp:107-127` lists only pike docs (`usage`, `keybindings`, `agent-lifecycle`, `runtime-capacities`, `architecture`); `src/coding_agent/prompt/BuiltinSlashCommands.cpp:29-32` explicitly drops `extensions` from `/reload`; `docs/usage.md` lists the supported agent files.
rows.cppEvidence: No C++ system-prompt text or built-in command claims package/extension loading or a `before_agent_start` hook. `/reload` currently lists keybindings, skills, prompts, themes and context files and omits extensions; that is an implementation gap for the selected native extension behavior, not a false positive claim. The only affected stale claim found is the C++ theme test wording `like pi` for unknown color tokens, which is false at v1.3.0 and belongs to the theme row.
rows.recommendation: Keep third-party package/TS-plugin claims absent. When the selected native extension behavior lands, update `/reload` and documentation only for the extension behavior actually implemented. Re-pin the theme test wording rather than adding a package surface.
